title: MEDI2004 W5 · Drug Targets
subject: Pharmacology Fundamentals
content: Four target classes (RITE): receptors, ion channels, enzymes, transporters. Three actions (AIM): activate, inhibit/block, modulate. Inhibitor stops the process; false substrate is processed into an abnormal product. Enzymes = reusable catalysts (-ase); AChE breaks down ACh (drug target; inhibit -> amplify signal). Anticholinesterases: reversible (donepezil, rivastigmine, pyridostigmine; Alzheimer's/myasthenia) vs irreversible (sarin, parathion; poisons, SLUDGE; atropine blocks muscarinic, pralidoxime reactivates AChE before aging). False substrates: methotrexate (DHFR), fluorouracil (thymidylate synthetase); block DNA synthesis; toxic to fast-dividing tissue; folinic acid rescue. Four receptor superfamilies (I Get Kinda Nervous): 1 ligand-gated ion channel (ionotropic; nicotinic ACh/GABA-A/NMDA; 4-5 subunits round pore; ms), 2 GPCR (7-TM; G-protein; s), 3 kinase-linked (insulin/GF/cytokines; dimerise+autophosphorylate; hours), 4 nuclear (steroid/thyroid; transcription factors; hours). Speed follows mechanism. GABA-A: GABA orthosteric, benzodiazepine allosteric (only enhances GABA, has ceiling), barbiturate opens channel directly (dangerous); flumazenil = BZ competitive antagonist. NMDA blockers: ketamine, memantine. G-protein cycle: agonist drives GDP->GTP (on), alpha GTPase hydrolyses GTP (off); Gs raises cAMP, Gi lowers, Gq->PLC. Desensitisation: GRK -> beta-arrestin -> internalisation -> tolerance; beta-blocker up-regulation -> rebound tachycardia. RTK: dimerise, autophosphorylate, Ras-Raf-MEK-MAPK -> transcription; cytokine JAK-STAT (SOCS brake). Nuclear receptors intracellular because ligands lipophilic; class I cytoplasm (HSP), class II nucleus; bind HRE (glucocorticoids, tamoxifen). Selectivity: subtypes (b1 vs b2), allosteric modulation (all families, safer/ceiling), functional selectivity/biased agonism (opioid analgesia via G-protein, respiratory depression via beta-arrestin; oliceridine). Transporters: carriers for poorly lipid-soluble solutes (renal tubule, gut, BBB). Passive (downhill) vs active (uphill); secondary symport/antiport on ion gradient; primary ATP (Na/K pump). SLC = facilitated uptake (SERT/NET/DAT); ABC = ATP efflux (P-glycoprotein -> poor absorption, BBB exclusion, multidrug resistance). Reuptake inhibitors: SSRIs (SERT), SNRIs (SERT+NET), TCAs; MAOIs block enzyme MAO; SSRI+MAOI -> serotonin syndrome.
